senses.definition: A device used to slow or stop the motion of a wheel, or of a vehicle, usually by friction (although other resistive forces, such as electromagnetic fields or aerodynamic drag, can also be used); also, the controls or apparatus used to engage such a mechanism such as the pedal in a car.
examples: She slammed the brakes when she saw a child run in front of the car.
You’re pressing the brakes too hard—try just squeezing them.

quotes.text: Auxiliaries and ancillaries are comprehensive, and include a Westinghouse motor-driven recriprocating compressor used for locomotive braking and general service air, two rotary exhauster sets for train brakes when hauling passenger or fitted freight trains, and an oil-fired train heating boiler.

subsenses.definition: The act of braking, of using a brake to slow down a machine or vehicle
examples: Give the car a quick brake.

subsenses.definition: (engineering) An apparatus for testing the power of a steam engine or other motor by weighing the amount of friction that the motor will overcome; a friction brake.
(figuratively) Something used to retard or stop some action, process etc.

senses.definition: (military) An ancient engine of war analogous to the crossbow and ballista.
(chiefly nautical) The handle of a pump.

senses.definition: A device used to confine or prevent the motion of an animal.

subsenses.definition: A frame for confining a refractory horse while the smith is shoeing it.
An enclosure to restrain cattle, horses, etc.
examples: He was shooting, and the field where the [cock-fighting] ring was verged on the shooting-brake where the rabbits were.

subsenses.definition: A cart or carriage without a body, used in breaking in horses.ᵂ
A carriage for transporting shooting parties and their equipment.ᵂ
